definitions.explanation: A person whose behavior, interests, or personality differs from what is considered normal or mainstream. Can be mildly negative or affectionately descriptive depending on context.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{少|すこ}し{変|か}わり{者|もの}だ。
examples.english: He's a bit of an oddball.

examples.japanese: {変|か}わり{者|もの}だと{思|おも}われても、{自分|じぶん}のスタイルを{貫|つらぬ}きたい。
examples.english: Even if people think I'm eccentric, I want to stick to my own style.

examples.japanese: うちの{教授|きょうじゅ}は{変|か}わり{者|もの}で{有名|ゆうめい}だけど、{授業|じゅぎょう}はとても{面白|おもしろ}い。
examples.english: Our professor is famous for being eccentric, but his classes are really interesting.

notes:
USAGE:
The tone depends heavily on context. It can be gently affectionate (describing a quirky but likeable person) or mildly critical (implying someone is hard to deal with). In Japanese society, which values conformity, being called a {変|か}わり{者|もの} is not necessarily a compliment, though it is not as harsh as {変人|へんじん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変|か}わり{者|もの}で{有名|ゆうめい} (famous for being eccentric)
- ちょっとした{変|か}わり{者|もの} (a bit of an eccentric)
- {変|か}わり{者|もの}だと{思|おも}われる (to be considered eccentric)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {変人|へんじん}: weirdo — more blunt and negative
- {個性的|こせいてき}: unique, individualistic — more positive framing
